policy.note: BITTERSWEET BW-002/BW-004. Every entry is a judgement a person made. `npm run m26:github:sync` refuses to emit a disposition that lacks a non-empty `reason` and a `verification` naming a command or a source path, and refuses any `verification` that is this script itself. An issue with no entry here stays OPEN as CARRY_FORWARD with pending_human_triage â€” it is never guessed and never silently closed.
policy.closures_are_destructive: Closing a GitHub issue is public and effectively irreversible from this repository. This file RECORDS the decision; it does not execute it. Applying the closures is a separate, explicitly approved step.
policy.labels_are_not_numbers: Keys are GitHub issue NUMBERS, not the MVP-###/CORE-###/M##-## labels. Those labels appear in the issue title. Guessing one from the other is how a closure gets aimed at the wrong issue.

classes.CLOSED_SHIPPED: The capability in the title exists in src/ AND is covered by a passing test.
classes.FIX_IN_BITTERSWEET: Maps to a numbered task in the BITTERSWEET release plan.
classes.CARRY_FORWARD: Real and wanted, not this release. Must name the blocking condition, not a milestone name.
classes.CLOSED_WONT_FIX: Contradicts a declared doctrine. Must cite the doctrine.
classes.CLOSED_BLOCKED_EXTERNAL: Real, but needs capacity or consent we do not have. Must cite a MATRIX-* cell with disposition BLOCKED.

NO_TELEMETRY.decision: MjÃ¶lnir ships no telemetry. Local-first is the product.
NO_TELEMETRY.rationale: A verification trust engine that reports on your test suite must not become a data-collection surface for that suite. The product is zero-network by contract and tests/contract/privacy-network-isolation.spec.ts enforces it. Telemetry cannot be added without breaking that contract, so a request for it is a request for a different product.

LOCAL_FIRST_NO_HOSTED_TIER.decision: There is no hosted control plane, air-gapped sync service, or hosted dashboard tier.
LOCAL_FIRST_NO_HOSTED_TIER.rationale: A hosted tier is a different product with a different threat model, a different consent story, and a different operational burden. The MATRIX-* cells stay BLOCKED, which is the honest representation and is cheaper than an issue backlog pretending they are planned.

223.reason: MVP-015 asks for a telemetry policy and event contract. DOCTRINE-NO-TELEMETRY settles it: the contract would describe an event stream the product will not have, and writing it invites someone to build the sender next.

224.reason: MVP-016 telemetry config plumbing. Refused by DOCTRINE-NO-TELEMETRY; config for a sender that must not exist is a config surface with no consumer.

225.reason: MVP-017 telemetry event builder with a privacy scrubber. A scrubber for an event stream that must not exist is the most dangerous kind of almost-feature: it makes the sink look built.

226.reason: MVP-018 `mjolnir telemetry inspect`. Refused by DOCTRINE-NO-TELEMETRY, and separately it would be a new verb, which the 5.x verb law forbids without a removal.

227.reason: MVP-019 telemetry send with a local queue and fail-open behaviour. A fail-open network sender is the exact opposite of this product's contract.

228.reason: MVP-020 telemetry first-run notice. A notice about a thing that never happens is noise in the first-run path, which is the one place the product has a user's full attention.

274.reason: CORE-036 telemetry product decision gate. The decision this gate was waiting for is now recorded in this file's doctrines block, so the gate has nothing left to wait for â€” this is the row that closes GAP-M26-014.

275.reason: CORE-037 telemetry privacy threat model. There is no telemetry to threaten; the threat model that matters here is enterprise/threat-model.json, which is validated in CI.

364.reason: CORE-126 asks for onboarding-friction telemetry ALTERNATIVES. Declining telemetry is not declining the underlying problem: measuring how hard onboarding is has a local answer (the existing scan artifacts) and needs a design decision about which local signals are worth reading, not a network sink.
364.deferred_because: the alternative measurement surface has not been designed; shipping a metric nobody has agreed to read is the same failure as shipping the telemetry
364.revisit_trigger: a local onboarding-friction measurement is specified and someone commits to reading it

150.reason: CORE-150 trust semantic diff. NOTE: the release plan cited `src/engine/change-intelligence.ts`, which no longer exists â€” it was deleted as an unshipped module. The `diff` capability actually ships as `diffAgainstBaseline` in the baseline command, which correlates findings by fingerprint (ruleId + file + message) rather than by line number.

112.reason: CORE-112 `mjolnir trust diff`. The verb is registered in the one command manifest and every registered verb is required to have a help page by a test.

180.reason: CORE-180 property-based and fuzz strategy. Ships as two dedicated Vitest configs wired to fast-check and run by ci-local.

141.reason: CORE-141 per-rule measured precision. Ships as a generated table consumed by the terminal's evidence descriptor, so a measured false-positive rate reaches the reader instead of living in a doc.

34.reason: CORE-034 memory profiling budget. Ships as the stress suite (soak + concurrent harnesses).

45.reason: CORE-045 path traversal / symlink containment. Ships as the atomic writer every artifact write goes through.

553.reason: M19-04 cancellable worker scheduler and resource budgets. The issue backlog and the engine work agree: the bounded pool and the honest `--max-duration` expiry contract are the same change, and neither is worth shipping alone.

292.reason: CORE-054 prove changed-scope impact analysis. Impact analysis is exactly the surface a wrong file selection silently corrupts: it looks authoritative and is wrong in a direction nobody can see.
292.deferred_because: no held-out differential evidence exists for change selection, so any impact number would be uncalibrated â€” shipping it would replace one false-green with another
292.revisit_trigger: a held-out corpus run reports selection precision and recall against a known-changed-file ground truth

595.reason: M22-09 prompt-injection, tool-poisoning and exfiltration red-team suite. The suite can be written today and would describe a threat model the runtime does not implement, because plugins execute with full Node privileges by design.
595.deferred_because: no plugin sandbox exists, so a red-team pass would certify a boundary that is not enforced anywhere
595.revisit_trigger: a plugin sandbox ships and a rule can be loaded into it

617.reason: M24-02 complete enterprise threat model and data-flow review â€” the only `release-blocker`-labelled open issue. Its own matrix cell already records the capability as BLOCKED, so completing the model cannot be done from this tree and does not block 5.0.
617.deferred_because: no consented air-gapped pilot and no least-privilege service account exist to model against
617.revisit_trigger: an offline enterprise pilot and recovery drill are run

232.reason: MVP-024 'management summary' artifact mode. Already delivered by the exec-report and trust-report surfaces. A dedicated verb would breach the 5.x verb law (one new verb requires one removal) for an output that already exists.
232.deferred_because: the capability is delivered by existing verbs; a dedicated verb is a naming preference, not a gap
232.revisit_trigger: the exec-report and trust-report surfaces measurably stop serving an executive audience
